evaluations.evidence: search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting
evaluations.rationale: “Content identification” vs “fingerprinting” and what inputs/sources are used (audio snippet, full track, humming, etc.) are underspecified and allow materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: based on my profile
evaluations.rationale: “My profile” is vague (listening history, demographics, explicit preferences, device context, etc.), leading to different requirement interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: based on other users similar to myself
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is undefined (taste similarity, demographics, behavior), enabling multiple materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” and “content similarity” are unclear (audio similarity, visual similarity, metadata similarity), yielding different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: exploiting enriched metadata and image tags ... related artists, new genre, or other relevant listening path
evaluations.rationale: “Enriched metadata,” “image tags,” and “relevant listening path” are broad abstractions that can be interpreted in materially different ways.

evaluations.evidence: upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps
evaluations.rationale: “Tags” (format, schema, who creates them) and “all further processing steps” are unclear, allowing different scope interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
evaluations.rationale: “Thumbnail sequences” and what constitutes a “video segment” (fixed length, shot boundaries, user-defined) are ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Info” and “similar” are undefined; similarity basis and information type can vary materially.

evaluations.evidence: info about perceptually similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Perceptually similar” is still underspecified (visual only, audio-visual, which perceptual features), enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: content recommendations from similar profiles
evaluations.rationale: “Content” and “similar profiles” are vague; both terms permit materially different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: based on most relevant news events in my area
evaluations.rationale: “Most relevant” and “my area” are ambiguous (radius, city, GPS; relevance criteria), leading to different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” could mean detect presence vs recognize identity; “related information” is unspecified, allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” (detect vs classify vs exact product match) and “related information” are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Identify” could mean detect logo presence vs determine broadcaster; “related information” is unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: “Brands” identification could be via logos, text, products; “related information” is vague.

evaluations.evidence: recommended with videos related to that picture or image
evaluations.rationale: “Related” is ambiguous (visual similarity, same subject, same location/event), leading to different recommendation behavior.

evaluations.evidence: be informed if there are videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest
evaluations.rationale: “Covering the area” and “relevant point of interest” are vague; notification conditions and relevance criteria are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: search content items using automatic speech recognition
evaluations.rationale: “Content items” and how ASR is used for search (query spoken by user vs indexing audio tracks) are ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation” is underspecified (shot boundaries, scenes, chapters, object segments), enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
evaluations.rationale: “Annotate” and “topic” are not defined (taxonomy, free-text, single vs multiple topics), allowing different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
evaluations.rationale: “A/V quality aspects” is vague (resolution, bitrate, loudness, artifacts, etc.), leading to different ranking criteria.

evaluations.evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
evaluations.rationale: “Quick assessment” and what counts as “edited” (cut, normalized, compressed, filtered) are ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter nudity content
evaluations.rationale: “Nudity content” is ambiguous (partial nudity, artistic nudity, context thresholds) and “prefilter” could mean block, flag, or deprioritize.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter content using search based on low­level asset information
evaluations.rationale: “Prefilter,” “content,” and “low-level asset information” are broad and can be interpreted in multiple materially different ways.

evaluations.evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
evaluations.rationale: “Validated” and “copyright infringement” detection scope (audio, video, images; matching method; thresholds) are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: high­level asset information such as metadata and tags either recognized by the system of provided by the user
evaluations.rationale: “High-level asset information” and “recognized by the system” are vague; also unclear what “prefilter” entails operationally.

evaluations.evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting,” “appealing,” and “complex” are subjective and allow materially different interpretations/metrics.

evaluations.evidence: detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should be prompted” and criteria for prompting are unclear; “subject” is also not defined in this story.

evaluations.evidence: identify volunteer types
evaluations.rationale: “Volunteer types” is undefined (skill level, behavior clusters, demographics, roles), enabling multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassify” and “simple low-level image features” are vague (which classes, which features), allowing different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: no classifiable animals
evaluations.rationale: “Classifiable animals” is ambiguous (no animals at all vs animals present but not identifiable), leading to different detection criteria.

evaluations.evidence: automatic image series detection for the case of timestamping malfunction
evaluations.rationale: “Image series detection” and what constitutes “timestamping malfunction” are underspecified, enabling different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal species preclassification
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassification” is unclear (suggested label vs filtering vs routing) and species set/taxonomy is unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal attribute preclassification
evaluations.rationale: “Attribute” is undefined (age, sex, behavior, markings, etc.) and “preclassification” is ambiguous in effect.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal number detection
evaluations.rationale: “Number detection” is ambiguous (exact count vs range vs presence/absence; per image vs per series).

evaluations.evidence: automatic segmentation or localization of plankton
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation” vs “localization” are different outputs and the story allows either, creating materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: no classifiable plankton
evaluations.rationale: “Classifiable plankton” is ambiguous (none present vs present but not identifiable), affecting detection requirements.

evaluations.evidence: detection of plankton size or orientation
evaluations.rationale: “Size” (area, length, scale calibration) and “orientation” (angle definition) are underspecified; “or” also permits different scopes.

evaluations.evidence: preclassification of plankton species
evaluations.rationale: “Preclassification” effect and the species taxonomy are not specified, allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: worm motion analysis to reduce video duration
evaluations.rationale: “Reduce video duration” is ambiguous (speed-up, trimming inactive segments, summarization) and “motion analysis” scope is unclear.

evaluations.evidence: detect the time ... where the worm lays an egg
evaluations.rationale: “The time” could mean timestamp, interval, or frame; detection granularity is ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc
evaluations.rationale: “Important features” is vague and the “etc” leaves scope open-ended, enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience
evaluations.rationale: “Probability/weight” and “experience” are undefined (what metric, how computed), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors
evaluations.rationale: “Artefacts” and “remove” are ambiguous (masking, filtering, discarding images) and examples don’t fully define scope.

evaluations.evidence: detect moving and transient objects
evaluations.rationale: “Transient objects” is unclear (duration threshold, types), leading to different detection requirements.

evaluations.evidence: remove background noise and distracting sounds
evaluations.rationale: “Background noise” and especially “distracting sounds” are subjective/undefined, enabling multiple interpretations of what to remove.

evaluations.evidence: group whale calls that are similar
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” is undefined (frequency patterns, call type, duration), allowing materially different grouping criteria.

evaluations.evidence: identify the number of whales heard
evaluations.rationale: “Number of whales heard” is ambiguous (distinct individuals vs overlapping calls; minimum/maximum estimate vs exact count).

evaluations.evidence: know when I should interrupt a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Interrupt” and the conditions for “should” are undefined, leading to different interpretations of triggers and actions.

evaluations.evidence: interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Still ambiguous what “interrupt” entails (modal, notification, blocking UI) and when it occurs; medium choice alone doesn’t define behavior.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should educate a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Educate” and criteria for “should” are unclear, allowing materially different interpretations of timing and content.

evaluations.evidence: educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “educate” means operationally and when it is triggered; multiple materially different behaviors fit.

evaluations.evidence: which piece of education I should give to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Piece of education” is undefined (lesson, tip, tutorial step) and selection criteria are unclear.

evaluations.evidence: interesting comment
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting” is subjective and undefined, enabling materially different detection/flagging criteria.

evaluations.evidence: when Zoonibot should comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Should comment” criteria and what constitutes a “subject” are unclear, allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: when Zoonibot should give an explanation
evaluations.rationale: “Explanation” and the conditions for “should” are underspecified, enabling multiple materially different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Should say” is open-ended without constraints (tone, templates, triggers, allowed content), leading to many interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: group subjects by similarity
evaluations.rationale: “Subjects” and “similarity” are undefined (feature basis, threshold), allowing materially different grouping requirements.

evaluations.evidence: recommend different projects ... based on their previous experiences
evaluations.rationale: “Previous experiences” is vague (projects joined, classifications made, performance, interests), enabling different recommendation logic.

evaluations.evidence: see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them
evaluations.rationale: “Summary” (length, fields, abstraction level) and “reuse them” (republish, reference, template) are ambiguous.
